lesson_scope: Geometric optimisation and modelling in one variable: forming models, domain constraints, stationary points, second-derivative tests, and answering fully.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: maximizing a quadratic area model and evaluating maximum value.

hints: Set the derivative equal to $0$: $40 - 4x = 0 \implies 4x = 40 \implies x = 10$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the area equation with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dA}{dx} = 40 - 4x$$

Set the derivative to zero to locate the stationary point:
$$40 - 4x = 0 \implies 4x = 40 \implies x = 10\text{ m}$$

Evaluate the maximum area:
$$A(10) = 40(10) - 2(10)^2 = 400 - 200 = 200\text{ m}^2$$
$$\text{Confirm maximum: } \frac{d^2A}{dx^2} = -4 < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $A = 40x - 2x^2$ to obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dx} = 40 - 4x$ and sets to $0$ to get $x = 10$.
Evaluates $A(10) = 200\text{ m}^2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: minimizing a rational perimeter model.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of minimising rational functions.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the perimeter function $P = 2x + 72x^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dP}{dx} = 2 - 72x^{-2} = 2 - \frac{72}{x^2}$$

Set the derivative equal to zero:
$$2 - \frac{72}{x^2} = 0 \implies 2x^2 = 72 \implies x^2 = 36$$

Select the physically valid positive root:
$$x = 6\text{ cm} \quad (\text{since } x > 0)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $P = 2x + 72x^{-1}$ to obtain $\dfrac{dP}{dx} = 2 - \dfrac{72}{x^2}$ and sets to $0$.
Solves $x^2 = 36$ with $x > 0$ to obtain $x = 6$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: perimeter constraint to area maximisation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of expressing single-variable area from linear constraint.

hints: Write area in terms of $x$: $A = x(12 - x) = 12x - x^2$.

walkthrough.text:
Express the area as a function of $x$:
$$A = x(12 - x) = 12x - x^2$$

Differentiate and set to zero:
$$\frac{dA}{dx} = 12 - 2x = 0 \implies 2x = 12 \implies x = 6\text{ cm}$$

Compute the maximum area:
$$A(6) = 12(6) - 6^2 = 72 - 36 = 36\text{ cm}^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms $A = 12x - x^2$, differentiates to $\dfrac{dA}{dx} = 12 - 2x$, and sets to $0$ to find $x = 6$.
Evaluates maximum area as $36\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: maximizing a cubic volume model.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of solving cubic volume stationary points.

hints: For $0 < x < 6$, the valid non-zero root is $x = 4$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume formula $V = 12x^2 - 2x^3$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 24x - 6x^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero and factorise:
$$6x(4 - x) = 0 \implies x = 0 \quad \text{or} \quad x = 4$$

Select the value inside $0 < x < 6$ and verify with second derivative:
$$x = 4\text{ cm}$$
$$\frac{d^2V}{dx^2} = 24 - 12x \implies \left.\frac{d^2V}{dx^2}\right|_{x=4} = 24 - 48 = -24 < 0 \implies \text{maximum}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates $V = 12x^2 - 2x^3$ to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx} = 24x - 6x^2$ and sets to $0$.
Selects the non-zero root $x = 4$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: minimizing a surface/cost model with reciprocal variable.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of cost function derivative involving pi and negative powers.

hints: Differentiate $C = 2\pi r^2 + 250r^{-1}$ with respect to $r$: $\dfrac{dC}{dr} = 4\pi r - 250r^{-2} = 4\pi r - \dfrac{250}{r^2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the cost function $C = 2\pi r^2 + 250r^{-1}$:
$$\frac{dC}{dr} = 4\pi r - \frac{250}{r^2}$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary point:
$$4\pi r - \frac{250}{r^2} = 0 \implies 4\pi r^3 = 250$$

Solve for $r^3$ in exact form:
$$r^3 = \frac{250}{4\pi} = \frac{125}{2\pi}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dC}{dr} = 4\pi r - \dfrac{250}{r^2}$ and sets to $0$.
Solves $4\pi r^3 = 250$ to obtain $r^3 = \dfrac{125}{2\pi}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: second derivative test justification for a maximum.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Foundational check of rigorous nature classification using second derivative test.

hints: Find $\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2} = -10$. Since $-10 < 0$, it is a maximum.

walkthrough.text:
Find the first derivative and set to zero:
$$\frac{dP}{dx} = 150 - 10x = 0 \implies 10x = 150 \implies x = 15$$

Compute the second derivative:
$$\frac{d^2P}{dx^2} = -10$$

State the conclusion:
$$\text{Since } \frac{d^2P}{dx^2} = -10 < 0 \text{ for all } x, \text{ the profit } P \text{ is maximized at } x = 15.$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to $\dfrac{dP}{dx} = 150 - 10x$ and solves $150 - 10x = 0$ to get $x = 15$.
Finds $\dfrac{d^2P}{dx^2} = -10 < 0$ to justify that it is a maximum.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: expanding a factored quadratic length model, setting the derivative to zero, and answering both optimal variable and optimal length value.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Direct quadratic optimisation with factored opening formula. This original prompt models length L = 3t(6-t) on 0 < t < 6.

walkthrough.text:
Expand the length model $L = 3t(6-t)$:
$$L = 18t - 3t^2$$

Differentiate with respect to $t$ and set to zero:
$$\frac{dL}{dt} = 18 - 6t = 0 \implies 6t = 18 \implies t = 3\text{ s}$$

Calculate the maximum length:
$$L_{\max} = 3(3)(6 - 3) = 9(3) = 27\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Justification: } \frac{d^2L}{dt^2} = -6 < 0 \implies \text{maximum}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Expands $L=18t-3t^2$.
Sets $\dfrac{dL}{dt}=18-6t$ equal to zero and obtains $t=3$.
States $L(3)=27\text{ cm}$ and that this is a maximum because $\dfrac{d^2L}{dt^2}=-6<0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Easy: forming a two-variable fencing model, eliminating one variable, differentiating a quadratic area formula, and retrieving both optimal compartment dimensions.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Establishing an area formula from a composite perimeter constraint with internal dividing fences. This original dog run uses 3 compartments in a row.

hints: With 3 compartments in a row, the outer perimeter and 2 dividers have 6 lengths of $x$ and 4 lengths of $y$: $6x + 4y = 80$.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the total fencing used for three compartments with width $x$ and depth $y$:
$$\text{Total fencing} = 6x + 4y = 80$$

Express $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$4y = 80 - 6x \implies y = 20 - \frac{3}{2}x$$

Express total area $A$ in terms of $x$:
$$A = 3xy = 3x\left(20 - \frac{3}{2}x\right) = 60x - \frac{9}{2}x^2$$

ai_rubric.observable: Forms the total area as $A=3xy$.
Uses the fencing constraint $6x+4y=80$ to obtain $y=20-\dfrac32x$ and the physical domain $0<x<\dfrac{40}{3}$.
Substitutes into $3xy$ and simplifies to the stated expression.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Differentiating the area formula to find optimal individual compartment dimensions.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the area formula $A = 60x - \frac{9}{2}x^2$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dA}{dx} = 60 - 9x$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the optimal width $x$:
$$60 - 9x = 0 \implies 9x = 60 \implies x = \frac{20}{3}\text{ m} \quad \left(6\frac{2}{3}\text{ m}\right)$$

Calculate the corresponding depth $y$ and confirm maximum:
$$y = 20 - \frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{20}{3}\right) = 20 - 10 = 10\text{ m}$$
$$\frac{d^2A}{dx^2} = -9 < 0 \implies \text{dimensions } x = \frac{20}{3}\text{ m}, \; y = 10\text{ m} \text{ maximize area.}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=60-9x$.
Solves $60-9x=0$ to obtain $x=\dfrac{20}{3}$, which lies in $0<x<\dfrac{40}{3}$.
Uses $y=20-\dfrac32x$ to obtain $y=10$ and identifies a maximum from $\dfrac{d^2A}{dx^2}=-9<0$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: two-part question on inscribed rectangle area under a parabola, requiring finding an exact surd stationary point and evaluating maximum area.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Inscribing a rectangle under a parabola y = 16 - x^2 and forming the cubic area model.

hints: The width of the rectangle is $x$ and the height is the $y$-coordinate on the curve: $y = 16 - x^2$.
Multiply width by height: $A = x(16 - x^2) = 16x - x^3$.

walkthrough.text: Identify the dimensions of the rectangle: base length is $x$ and height is $y = 16 - x^2$.

Form the area expression:
$$A = \text{base} \times \text{height} = x(16 - x^2) = 16x - x^3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies the rectangle height as $16-x^2$.
Multiplies width $x$ by height $16-x^2$ and expands.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding the exact maximum area of the inscribed rectangle.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the area formula $A = 16x - x^3$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dA}{dx} = 16 - 3x^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary point for $0 < x < 4$:
$$16 - 3x^2 = 0 \implies x^2 = \frac{16}{3} \implies x = \frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}$$

Calculate the maximum area in exact form:
$$A_{\max} = 16\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right) - \left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^3 = \frac{64}{\sqrt{3}} - \frac{64}{3\sqrt{3}} = \frac{192 - 64}{3\sqrt{3}} = \frac{128}{3\sqrt{3}} \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{128\sqrt{3}}{9}\right)$$
$$\text{Justify maximum: } \frac{d^2A}{dx^2} = -6x = -6\left(\frac{4}{\sqrt{3}}\right) < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dA}{dx}=16-3x^2$.
Solves $16-3x^2=0$ in $0<x<4$ to obtain $x=\dfrac4{\sqrt3}$.
Uses $A''=-6x<0$ at this value and evaluates $A=\dfrac{128}{3\sqrt3}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: pyramid volume model from linear constraint h + 2x = 24, finding optimal x, corresponding h, and maximum volume.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Pyramid volume model with linear relation h + 2x = 24, full optimisation workflow.

hints: Volume of a square pyramid is $V = \dfrac{1}{3}x^2 h$.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $h = 24 - 2x$ into the pyramid volume formula $V = \frac{1}{3}x^2 h$:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}x^2 (24 - 2x) = 8x^2 - \frac{2}{3}x^3$$

Differentiate with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 16x - 2x^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary point for $0 < x < 12$:
$$2x(8 - x) = 0 \implies x = 8\text{ cm}$$

Find the corresponding height $h$ and maximum volume:
$$h = 24 - 2(8) = 8\text{ cm}$$
$$V_{\max} = \frac{1}{3}(8^2)(8) = \frac{512}{3}\text{ cm}^3 \quad \left(170\frac{2}{3}\text{ cm}^3\right)$$
$$\text{Confirm maximum: } \frac{d^2V}{dx^2} = 16 - 4x \implies \left.\frac{d^2V}{dx^2}\right|_{x=8} = 16 - 32 = -16 < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses $h=24-2x$ and writes $V=\dfrac13x^2(24-2x)=8x^2-\dfrac23x^3$.
Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=16x-2x^2$.
Solves the non-zero stationary value as $x=8$ and obtains $h=8$.
Shows $\dfrac{d^2V}{dx^2}=16-4x=-16<0$ at $x=8$.
Substitutes to state $V_{\max}=\dfrac{512}{3}\text{ cm}^3$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Medium: right triangle area model with square root, using squaring trick B = A^2 to find maximum area cleanly.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Pythagoras on right triangle with hypotenuse 10 cm leading to radical area model.

walkthrough.text:
Apply Pythagoras' theorem to express the perpendicular side $y$ in terms of $x$:
$$x^2 + y^2 = 10^2 = 100 \implies y = \sqrt{100 - x^2}$$

Substitute $y$ into the triangle area formula $A = \frac{1}{2}xy$:
$$A = \frac{1}{2}x\sqrt{100 - x^2}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses Pythagoras to obtain $y^2=100-x^2$.
Takes the positive root and substitutes into $A=\dfrac12xy$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Maximising the triangle area via stationary point analysis.

hints: Since $A \ge 0$, maximizing $A$ is equivalent to maximizing $B = A^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}x^2(100 - x^2) = 25x^2 - \dfrac{1}{4}x^4$.
Differentiate $B$: $B' = 50x - x^3 = x(50 - x^2) = 0 \implies x^2 = 50 \implies x = 5\sqrt{2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Maximizing non-negative $A$ is equivalent to maximizing $B = A^2$:
$$B = A^2 = \frac{1}{4}x^2(100 - x^2) = 25x^2 - \frac{1}{4}x^4$$

Differentiate $B$ with respect to $x$ and set to zero:
$$\frac{dB}{dx} = 50x - x^3 = x(50 - x^2) = 0 \implies x = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$$

Compute the corresponding side $y$ and the maximum area:
$$y = \sqrt{100 - (5\sqrt{2})^2} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ cm}$$
$$A_{\max} = \frac{1}{2}(5\sqrt{2})(5\sqrt{2}) = \frac{1}{2}(50) = 25\text{ cm}^2$$
$$\text{Confirm maximum: } \frac{d^2B}{dx^2} = 50 - 3x^2 \implies \left.\frac{d^2B}{dx^2}\right|_{x=5\sqrt{2}} = 50 - 150 = -100 < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: States that $A\ge0$, so maximizing $A$ is equivalent to maximizing $B=A^2=\dfrac14x^2(100-x^2)=25x^2-\dfrac14x^4$.
Differentiates $B$ to obtain $B'=50x-x^3$ and solves the non-zero stationary value as $x=5\sqrt2$.
Shows $B''=50-3x^2=-100<0$ at this value and uses $y=5\sqrt2$ to state $A=25\text{ cm}^2$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: open box from rectangular net, requiring forming cubic volume model, solving quadratic derivative for exact surd root in the valid domain, and testing nature.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Forming open box volume V = x(20-2x)(12-2x) from folded sheet.

hints: When corners of side $x$ are removed, the base has dimensions $(20 - 2x)$ and $(12 - 2x)$, and height is $x$.

walkthrough.text: Identify the dimensions of the folded box: base length is $(20 - 2x)\text{ cm}$, base width is $(12 - 2x)\text{ cm}$, and height is $x\text{ cm}$.

Multiply the dimensions to express the volume $V$:
$$V = x(20 - 2x)(12 - 2x)$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the folded-box dimensions $x$, $20-2x$ and $12-2x$.
Expands and simplifies to the stated cubic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Maximising box volume by solving quadratic derivative in exact surd form.

hints: Since $0 < x < 6$, choose the minus root: $x = \dfrac{16 - 2\sqrt{19}}{3}\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume formula $V = 240x - 64x^2 + 4x^3$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 240 - 128x + 12x^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero and simplify by dividing by $4$:
$$12x^2 - 128x + 240 = 0 \implies 3x^2 - 32x + 60 = 0$$

Solve using the quadratic formula:
$$x = \frac{32 \pm \sqrt{(-32)^2 - 4(3)(60)}}{2(3)} = \frac{32 \pm \sqrt{1024 - 720}}{6} = \frac{32 \pm \sqrt{304}}{6}$$
$$x = \frac{32 \pm 4\sqrt{19}}{6} = \frac{16 \pm 2\sqrt{19}}{3}$$

Select the root that satisfies the physical constraint $0 < x < 6$:
$$\text{Since } \frac{16 + 2\sqrt{19}}{3} \approx 8.24 > 6, \text{ the valid root is } x = \frac{16 - 2\sqrt{19}}{3}\text{ cm} \quad (\approx 2.43\text{ cm})$$
$$\text{Confirm maximum: } \frac{d^2V}{dx^2} = -128 + 24x = -128 + 8(16 - 2\sqrt{19}) = -16\sqrt{19} < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=240-128x+12x^2$.
Solves $240-128x+12x^2=0$ and selects the only root in $0<x<6$, $x=\dfrac{16-2\sqrt{19}}{3}$.
Shows $\dfrac{d^2V}{dx^2}=-128+24x<0$ at this root, so the volume is a maximum.

questions.difficulty_reason: Hard: lidless box volume model from surface area constraint S = 72, finding exact surd optimal dimensions and maximum volume.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Surface area constraint x^2 + 4xh = 72 on open box leading to cubic volume model.

hints: A lidless box has 1 base and 4 vertical sides: $S = x^2 + 4xh = 72$.
Express $h$ in terms of $x$: $4xh = 72 - x^2 \implies h = \dfrac{72 - x^2}{4x}$.
Substitute into $V = x^2 h$: $V = x^2\left(\dfrac{72 - x^2}{4x}\right) = \dfrac{x(72 - x^2)}{4} = 18x - \dfrac{1}{4}x^3$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the surface area equation for the lidless box (one square base of side $x$ and four sides of dimensions $x \times h$):
$$S = x^2 + 4xh = 72$$

Rearrange for the height $h$:
$$4xh = 72 - x^2 \implies h = \frac{72 - x^2}{4x}$$

Substitute $h$ into the volume formula $V = x^2 h$:
$$V = x^2 \left(\frac{72 - x^2}{4x}\right) = \frac{x(72 - x^2)}{4} = 18x - \frac{1}{4}x^3$$

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the material constraint $x^2+4xh=72$.
Rearranges it to obtain $h=\dfrac{72-x^2}{4x}$.
Substitutes into $V=x^2h$ and simplifies to the stated cubic.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Finding optimal dimensions and exact maximum volume of the lidless box.

hints: Set to zero: $18 - \dfrac{3}{4}x^2 = 0 \implies \dfrac{3}{4}x^2 = 18 \implies x^2 = 24 \implies x = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$.

walkthrough.text:
Differentiate the volume formula $V = 18x - \frac{1}{4}x^3$ with respect to $x$:
$$\frac{dV}{dx} = 18 - \frac{3}{4}x^2$$

Set the derivative equal to zero to find the stationary point for $0 < x < \sqrt{72}$:
$$18 - \frac{3}{4}x^2 = 0 \implies \frac{3}{4}x^2 = 18 \implies x^2 = 24 \implies x = \sqrt{24} = 2\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the corresponding height $h$:
$$h = \frac{72 - (2\sqrt{6})^2}{4(2\sqrt{6})} = \frac{72 - 24}{8\sqrt{6}} = \frac{48}{8\sqrt{6}} = \frac{6}{\sqrt{6}} = \sqrt{6}\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the maximum volume in exact surd form:
$$V_{\max} = x^2 h = (24)(\sqrt{6}) = 24\sqrt{6}\text{ cm}^3$$
$$\text{Confirm maximum: } \frac{d^2V}{dx^2} = -\frac{3}{2}x \implies \left.\frac{d^2V}{dx^2}\right|_{x=2\sqrt{6}} = -3\sqrt{6} < 0$$

ai_rubric.observable: Differentiates to obtain $\dfrac{dV}{dx}=18-\dfrac34x^2$.
Solves for the positive stationary value $x=2\sqrt6$.
Uses the area constraint to obtain $h=\sqrt6$.
Shows $\dfrac{d^2V}{dx^2}=-\dfrac32x<0$ at this value and states $V=24\sqrt6\text{ cm}^3$.
